## Purpose and Entry Points
A Go-based Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing Terraform Registry and HCP Terraform/Terraform Enterprise capabilities to MCP clients. The primary executable is `cmd/terraform-mcp-server/main.go`; initialization, CLI/environment setup, and transport selection are in `cmd/terraform-mcp-server/init.go`. It runs over stdio JSON-RPC by default or Streamable HTTP for remote deployments.

## Server Composition and Transport
The command layer constructs the MCP server, attaches instructions/resources/tools, and starts either stdio or HTTP serving. HTTP supports `/mcp` plus health handling, TLS, CORS, keep-alive/SSE, and stateful versus stateless sessions. The official MCP-facing implementation is organized under `pkg/mcp-official/server.go`, with HTTP/session client behavior in `pkg/mcp-official/client/http_client.go` and `pkg/mcp-official/client/session.go`.

## Tool Registration and Exposure Control
Tools are assembled from factories and exposed according to named toolsets or explicit tool lists. `pkg/tools/tools.go` is the tool aggregation boundary; `pkg/tools/factories.go` creates tool instances; `pkg/toolsets/mapping.go` maps user-facing toolsets (`registry`, `terraform`, private registry, etc.) to individual tools. This separates protocol registration from API-specific tool implementation and prevents conflicting `--tools`/`--toolsets` selections.

## Registry Tool Domain
Public Terraform Registry operations—provider/module/policy discovery, metadata, capabilities, and latest versions—live in `pkg/tools/registry/`. Representative paths are `pkg/tools/registry/search_modules.go`, `pkg/tools/registry/get_provider_details.go`, and `pkg/tools/registry/get_latest_module_version.go`. These tools invoke Registry client abstractions rather than directly owning transport/auth concerns.

## HCP Terraform / Terraform Enterprise Tool Domain
`pkg/tools/tfe/` implements the larger authenticated management surface: organizations, projects, workspaces, teams, runs/plans/applies, state versions, policy/variable sets, and private registry queries. Examples: `pkg/tools/tfe/create_workspace.go`, `pkg/tools/tfe/create_run.go`, and `pkg/tools/tfe/get_plan_json_output.go`. Potentially mutating Terraform operations are gated by the explicit operations-enable setting, forming an approval/safety boundary.

## API Clients, Credentials, and Request Policy
`pkg/client/` centralizes configuration, token resolution, TLS behavior, HTTP middleware, Registry access, and TFE API access: `pkg/client/config.go`, `pkg/client/registry_client.go`, and `pkg/client/tfe_client.go`. In HTTP mode, request-scoped bearer/TFE tokens support centralized per-user RBAC; server-side TFE address remains fixed. Middleware enforces organization allowlists, global/per-session rate limits, tool-call logging, and metrics (`pkg/client/org_allowlist_tool_middleware.go`, `pkg/client/ratelimit.go`, `pkg/client/tool_logging_middleware.go`).

## Resources, Observability, and Deployment
MCP resources and templates are supplied from `pkg/resources/resources.go` and `pkg/resources/resource_templates.go`; default agent instructions are `cmd/terraform-mcp-server/instructions.md`. OpenTelemetry tool/server metrics and optional Instana instrumentation are configured at the command/server layers, with official middleware in `pkg/mcp-official/tools/middleware/metrics.go`. Distribution targets are a container (`Dockerfile`) and Kubernetes Helm deployment (`helm/terraform-mcp-server/templates/deployment.yaml`), with external dependencies being Terraform Registry, HCP Terraform/TFE APIs, optional OTel collector, and optional Instana agent.
